STATUS: NOT SET AS DEFAULT LAUNCHER
Threshold removes app grids, notification badges and feeds, providing just a plain, undistracting, minimal surface. It turns your phone into a precision tool, rather than an attention trap.
No colourful app icons, unread counters, or infinite home screen pages.
Restricted apps are filtered cleanly at the launch surface without invasive background services.
Zero internet permissions and zero telemetry. Every rule resides locally on your device.
Type what you intend to open.
Tap the search prompt on the home canvas to filter installed apps instantly, or pin up to 7 essential daily utilities beneath search.
Type a few letters of any allowed app to launch with zero delay.
Pin your most-used tools directly below search for immediate one-tap access.
Type :settings to open configuration or :wallpaper to apply a solid black wallpaper.
Assign every app to Allow, Guard, or Block. Tap the mechanical toggle below to feel the micro-haptic detent for each tier:
ALLOW: Launches immediately from search and quick actions with zero delay.
GUARD: Pauses launch behind a deliberate cognitive checkpoint before opening.
BLOCK: Hidden from search results and disabled in quick actions.
Transcribe a randomized mindfulness phrase character-for-character (e.g. \"I am opening Social Feed intentionally\") to unlock launch.
Drag geometric glyph pairs into their matching target slots with tactile snap detents.
Trace the Threshold caret steadily across its perimeter—releasing early resets the countdown.
Dynamically selects a different cognitive checkpoint on every launch attempt.
Rules that adapt to time, space, and hardware.
Layer custom profiles such as Deep Work or Bedtime above your base configuration. Profiles evaluate in priority order using AND / OR combinations of reusable triggers:
Activate profiles automatically during recurring daily or overnight time windows.
Switch rules automatically when you are inside or outside a saved location such as Home or Office.
Tap a physical NFC tag to latch a profile on/off or start a timed session with daily tap limits.
Threshold keeps settings out of sight during daily use and provides optional self-binding commitment locks when you want to prevent impulse edits:
Press and hold on the home canvas for 3 seconds (or type :settings in search) to open Settings.
When enabled in Settings, any future edits to rules or profiles are staged and only take effect after a full device restart.
Power users can lock and unlock all configuration changes completely via ADB broadcast.

To serve as your home screen and intent gatekeeper, Threshold must hold the system Default Home App role. If Threshold is not set as your default launcher, this wizard will run again next time you open the app.
Require full typing of guarded apps
Changes to settings, apps, profiles, and triggers take effect after device restart
Enables Threshold Hardened Mode for OS-level package suspension and tamper resistance.
Threshold holds Device Owner privileges. Blocked apps are suspended at the OS level and launcher self-protection is active.

Threshold is running as a standard intent gatekeeper. Blocked apps are hidden from Threshold\'s launcher surfaces, but can still be opened via the Android Recents switcher, notifications, or external deep links.

Suspends Blocked apps in the Android OS (setPackagesSuspended). If a Blocked app is running when a profile activates, Android closes it immediately, silences its notifications, and blocks re-entry from Recents or links. Guarded apps remain unsuspended so their notifications arrive normally.
Locks Threshold as the persistent system Home app so the stock launcher cannot be re-selected in Android System Settings to bypass your rules.
Disables Uninstall, Force Stop, and Clear Storage for Threshold in Android System Settings while Hardened Mode is active.
Hardened Mode closes Android OS escape hatches. Pair it with Threshold\'s Settings locks so rules cannot be weakened from inside Threshold:
Stages any edits to app rules, profiles, or triggers in Settings until you restart your phone.
Completely locks Threshold Settings from being opened on the phone until unlocked from a computer.

Hardened Mode cannot be toggled from inside Threshold\'s normal menus. You can enable or disable it either by scanning the QR codes on the Threshold website or via USB debugging (ADB) from a computer.
Recommended Only for New or Freshly Reset Devices

We strongly recommend enabling Hardened Mode only on a brand-new or freshly reset phone before signing into your accounts.\n\nWe do NOT recommend enabling Hardened Mode on a phone where your accounts are already set up: Android blocks Device Owner activation whenever Google accounts, Work Profiles, or Private Spaces are present, and removing an existing Google account can wipe Google Wallet contactless cards or sign you out of apps. On an existing phone, use Require Reboot for Settings Changes and the ADB Settings Lock below instead.
Option A: QR Code Setup & Removal (No Computer Required)

• To Enable on a Freshly Reset Phone: On Android\'s very first Welcome screen after a factory reset, tap the screen 6 times in the same spot to open Android\'s QR scanner, then scan the Hardened Mode Setup QR code on the Threshold website.\n• To Disable Hardened Mode: Scan the Hardened Mode Deactivation QR code on the Threshold website with your phone\'s Camera app to open the hidden deactivation screen.
2. Disable Hardened Mode (Unsuspends Apps & Releases Device Owner)

Disabling Hardened Mode will immediately:

• Unsuspend all Blocked apps in the Android OS
• Unlock Default Home App selection, Force Stop, Clear Storage, and Uninstall for Threshold
• Permanently release Device Owner privileges (re-enabling Hardened Mode later requires a freshly reset device)
Hardened Mode (Device Owner) is not currently active on this device.
Once enabled, any future changes to settings, app rules, profiles, or triggers—including turning this setting off—will only take effect after you restart your device.
Restart your device to apply staged changes to active settings.
Apply solid AMOLED black to system and lock screen
This will replace your current system and lock screen wallpaper with solid AMOLED black.
